Amazon officially opened its first Puerto Rico delivery station on Nov. 16 in Dorado. The company says customers across the San Juan metro area can now receive packages in about two days, compared with waits of up to two weeks before the station began making deliveries.
What’s Related
The 100,000-square-foot station began delivering packages in August, three months before the formal opening. It’s Amazon’s first logistics facility in the Caribbean. Puerto Rico Gov. Jenniffer González-Colón and Dorado Mayor Aníbal José Torres attended the opening.
The station employs more than 100 people, and six independent delivery companies based there account for about 300 additional driver roles, Amazon said. Hiring is still underway ahead of the holiday shopping season .
RELATED: Ranking the Top 50 Global Third-Party Logistics Providers
How packages move through Dorado
The Dorado station handles the last step before packages reach customers. Workers receive incoming parcels, sort them by delivery route, and load them into vans. Amazon says doing that work locally gives it a faster way to get packages to homes and businesses around San Juan.
The roughly two-day estimate applies to the San Juan metro area. Amazon’s announcement leaves open which ZIP codes qualify for faster delivery and how many packages the station can handle each day.
Six delivery companies operate from the site
The six companies are part of Amazon’s Delivery Service Partner program. They pick up packages at the Dorado station and handle the final leg to the customer. Under the program, the delivery companies hire and manage their own drivers, while Amazon provides technology that plans routes based on factors such as package volume and delivery addresses.
Early estimates put the number of driving jobs at about 200 when plans for the station were reported in 2024. Amazon put that figure at about 300 at the formal opening. The estimated number of jobs inside the station was about 100 in 2024, close to the staffing level Amazon reported in November.
